sections.title: The Righteousness of Faith
observations: In this section, Paul emphasizes that righteousness comes through faith, not through the law. He contrasts the righteousness that is based on the law with the righteousness that is based on faith in Christ.
Paul quotes from Deuteronomy to illustrate that the message of faith is accessible and not distant or unattainable. It is a call to believe in the heart and confess with the mouth.

sections.title: The Importance of Preaching the Gospel
observations: Paul stresses the necessity of preaching the gospel for salvation. He highlights that faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.
This section underscores the role of evangelism and the importance of sharing the message of salvation with others.

sections.title: Israel's Unbelief
observations: Paul addresses the issue of Israel's rejection of the gospel. He expresses his sorrow for his fellow Israelites who have not accepted Christ despite their zeal for God.
He explains that their zeal is not based on knowledge, as they sought to establish their own righteousness rather than submitting to God's righteousness.

importantVerses.commentary: If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. This verse encapsulates the essence of the gospel and the simplicity of salvation through faith.
For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. This verse emphasizes the universal offer of salvation to all who believe, highlighting God's grace and mercy.

questions: What does it mean to confess Jesus as Lord in the context of salvation?
How does Paul’s teaching on faith and works challenge our understanding of righteousness?
In what ways can we actively participate in sharing the gospel as Paul describes?
